skill.name: webapp-testing
skill.description: Toolkit for interacting with and testing local web applications using Playwright. Supports verifying frontend functionality, debugging UI behavior, capturing browser screenshots, and viewing browser logs.

security_audit.summary: Two subprocess findings are confirmed because the helper executes supplied server strings and command arguments. The other 28 detections are benign local examples, artifact writes, or Markdown syntax. SKILL.md also discourages source review before execution, creating a high-severity prompt-injection and supply-chain risk.

remediation.issue: The server helper passes supplied server strings directly to a shell and runs an unrestricted follow-up command.
remediation.suggestion: Use structured executable arguments and working directories, remove shell=True, validate commands, and require confirmation before launching external processes.

remediation.issue: The skill tells agents to execute bundled scripts before reviewing their source and to treat them as black boxes.
remediation.suggestion: Remove this instruction and require source inspection, provenance verification, and explicit command review before any bundled script runs.

content.user_title: Test Local Web Apps with Playwright
content.value_statement: Testing local interfaces requires reliable server startup, browser inspection, and artifact capture. This skill provides Playwright patterns and a server lifecycle helper.
actual_capabilities: Guides synchronous Playwright scripts for local dynamic applications and static HTML files.
Starts one or more local development servers and waits for configured ports.
Runs a browser automation command after local servers become available.
Discovers visible buttons, links, and form controls from rendered pages.
Captures full-page screenshots and browser console messages as test artifacts.
Uses rendered-state inspection before selecting and performing browser actions.
limitations: Requires Python, Playwright, and a compatible Chromium installation.
Targets local applications and local HTML files, not hosted browser infrastructure.
Example URLs, paths, selectors, and interactions require project-specific changes.
The server helper executes supplied commands, so every command must be trusted and reviewed.

use_cases.title: Debug a Local Frontend
use_cases.description: Inspect the rendered interface, capture console messages, and verify interactions while a local development server runs.

use_cases.title: Run Repeatable UI Checks
use_cases.description: Automate a focused user workflow and collect screenshots or browser logs for defect investigation.

use_cases.title: Inspect a Static Prototype
use_cases.description: Open a local HTML file, identify useful selectors, exercise controls, and record visual results.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Local Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [local URL] with Playwright, wait for the page to settle, capture a full-page screenshot, and summarize visible errors.

prompt_templates.title: Discover Interactive Elements
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [local URL] and list visible buttons, links, inputs, and stable selectors. Capture browser console warnings and errors.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a User Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Test this workflow on [local URL]: [steps]. Report each result, relevant console errors, and the saved screenshot locations.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Multi-Service Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these trusted startup commands: [commands]. Start each local service, wait for [ports], run [workflow], collect evidence, and stop every process.

output_examples.input: Inspect the dashboard and report available actions.
output: Found 6 visible buttons, 4 links, and 2 form fields.
Stable labels include Create report, Refresh data, and Open settings.
Saved a full-page screenshot to the approved output directory.

output_examples.input: Test sign-in validation with an empty password.
output: The form stayed on the sign-in page.
A password-required message appeared below the password field.
No new browser console errors were observed.

output_examples.input: Capture browser errors after opening the local application.
output: Captured one failed resource request and one application warning.
Saved the console transcript for review.

best_practices: Review helper source and every command string before starting local processes.
Wait for an appropriate page state before inspecting elements or performing actions.
Close browsers and child processes, then store artifacts only in approved locations.
anti_patterns: Do not pass untrusted text to the server helper because server strings reach a shell.
Do not run tests against production systems or real user data without explicit authorization.
Do not reuse fixed example selectors, paths, or waits without validating the current interface.

faq.question: What applications can this skill test?
faq.answer: It supports local dynamic web applications and local static HTML files through Playwright.

faq.question: What software is required?
faq.answer: Python, Playwright, and an installed compatible Chromium browser are required.

faq.question: Can it start multiple local services?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper can start several server commands and wait for each configured port.

faq.question: What evidence can it collect?
faq.answer: The examples collect screenshots, visible element details, link targets, and browser console messages.

faq.question: Is it intended for production testing?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflows target local applications and require separate safeguards for remote or production systems.

faq.question: Why do commands require review?
faq.answer: The helper accepts server strings through a shell and runs a supplied command after startup.
